proof.text: Let $F=F_X$ be the strict tuple functor specified in [def-coef-complete-algebroid]. Every $X^{n+1}$ is Kan by filling horns in each coordinate. Apply [lem-coef-kan-relative-nerve-left-fibration] to the small ordinary category $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ and this $F$. Its specified relative nerve $E=\Delta_X^{\mathrm{op}}$ is a left and cocartesian fibration, every edge is cocartesian, its fiber over $[n]$ is $X^{n+1}$, and its transport along $\phi$ is $F(\phi)$. In particular the degree-zero fiber is $X$ and is Kan. For an inert projection choose the edge with constant path at the projected tuple; the relative-nerve formula gives that edge, and the theorem makes it cocartesian. Left horn lifting includes inner horn lifting, so $E\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ is an inner fibration as required.

proof.text:
Write $v_j$ for the projection onto vertex $j$ and $e_i$ for the projection onto the edge $(i-1,i)$. The category $I_n$ in [lem-coef-operadic-algebra-presentability] has exactly the arrows $e_i\to v_{i-1},v_i$, besides identities. The fiber diagram has value $X$ at each $v_j$ and $X\times X$ at each $e_i$, with coordinate projections. Its ordinary limit is $X^{n+1}$: matching pairs are uniquely the list $(x_0,\ldots,x_n)$.
To check the limit in spaces, use the end model of [def-coef-rectified-space-limit]. Put $T_j=N(I_n/v_j)$; this is a star with one terminal vertex $\mathrm{id}_{v_j}$ and one incoming edge for each incident $e_i$. Since $I_n/e_i$ is a point, the end conditions say precisely that each coordinate of the point assigned at $e_i$ is the restriction of a map $T_j\to X$ at its corresponding leaf. Thus the end is isomorphic, in every simplicial degree, to $\prod_{j=0}^n\operatorname{Fun}(T_j,X)$. Evaluation at the terminal vertices retracts this onto $X^{n+1}$. Its section is the constant-map inclusion. The natural transformation from the identity functor of each star to its terminal constant functor supplies $T_j\times\Delta^1\to T_j$; precomposition supplies a simplicial homotopy between the identity and section followed by retraction. Hence the canonical cone is limiting. This is the same matching diagram as the iterated fiber product of the consecutive edge fibers over shared vertex fibers, and proves the required Segal equivalence. For $n=0$, $I_0$ has just $v_0$, the zero-edge product is $X$, and the comparison is its identity.

source.place: Definition 2.1; coordinate verification of the generalized-operad assertion, following Gepner–Haugseng, arXiv:1312.3178, Definition 3.1.13 and Remarks 4.1.2–4.1.4.

proof.text: Fix $\phi:[m]\to[n]$, $a\in X^{m+1}$, and $b\in X^{n+1}$, and put $c=F(\phi)a$. Use the right-pinched mapping-space definition of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. An $r$-simplex over $\phi$ has base the nerve simplex with $r+1$ initial copies of $[m]$, identity arrows between them, followed by $\phi$ to $[n]$. In the relative-nerve description of [def-coef-complete-algebroid], all $t_J$ for $J\subseteq\{0,\ldots,r\}$ are the constant simplex at $a$. All $t_J$ containing the last vertex are restrictions of the single map $t_{\{0,\ldots,r+1\}}:\Delta^{r+1}\to X^{n+1}$. Its initial face is constant at $c$ and its last vertex is $b$. Conversely every such map gives all the required $t_J$ by these formulas; compatibility for an inclusion not containing the last vertex is exactly the initial-face condition. Restriction commutes with the extended simplex operators. We therefore obtain an isomorphism of simplicial sets $\operatorname{Map}_E^\phi(a,b)\cong\operatorname{Map}_{X^{n+1}}(c,b)$. The base mapping space is the discrete set of arrows of $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$, so its homotopy fiber at $\phi$ is modeled by this strict fiber: a path in that discrete set is necessarily constant.

source.place: Definition 2.1; coordinate verification of the generalized-operad assertion, following Gepner–Haugseng, arXiv:1312.3178, Definition 3.1.13 and Remarks 4.1.2–4.1.4.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison] to the Kan complex $X^{n+1}$, regarded as a quasicategory, with endpoints $c,b$. It identifies the mapping space of step 3 by a natural homotopy equivalence with the endpoint-fixed path space $P_{c,b}(X^{n+1})$. Internal functor simplicial sets and endpoint conditions are coordinatewise, so this path space is isomorphic to $\prod_{j=0}^nY_j$, where $Y_j=P_{c_j,b_j}(X)$. These are Kan by the same pinch-comparison statement. Under the chosen inert projections, step 3 sends a simplex $t$ to its corresponding coordinate subtuple. Indeed the relative-nerve triangle composing with the constant projection edge is obtained by applying that coordinate projection to $t$ and repeating its last vertex. Naturality of the pinch map therefore identifies the entire incidence diagram, including its arrows, with the diagram having $Y_j$ at $v_j$ and $Y_{i-1}\times Y_i$ at $e_i$, with the two projections. This checks the comparison maps, rather than merely identifying the individual mapping spaces.

source.place: Definition 2.1; coordinate verification of the generalized-operad assertion, following Gepner–Haugseng, arXiv:1312.3178, Definition 3.1.13 and Remarks 4.1.2–4.1.4.

proof.text: Compute the limit of this Kan-valued incidence diagram using [def-coef-rectified-space-limit]. An element of its end consists of a map $T_j=N(I_n/v_j)\to Y_j$ for each $j$, and at each $e_i$ a pair of points in $Y_{i-1}\times Y_i$ whose coordinates are the restrictions at the two corresponding leaves. Hence those pairs are uniquely determined and the end is isomorphic to $\prod_j\operatorname{Fun}(T_j,Y_j)$, with all simplicial parameters retained. The canonical comparison from $\prod_jY_j$ is exactly the product of constant-map inclusions. Evaluate each map at $\mathrm{id}_{v_j}$ to get its retraction. Precomposition with the simplicial contraction induced by the arrows of $I_n/v_j$ into $\mathrm{id}_{v_j}$ gives a homotopy from the identity to constant extension of this evaluation. Thus this comparison is a homotopy equivalence. By step 4 the apex is $P_{F(\phi)a,b}(X^{n+1})$, and its cone is the canonical cone of mapping spaces over the inert composites $\alpha\phi$. This proves the incidence axiom in the exact convention of [lem-coef-operadic-algebra-presentability]. When $n=0$ the sole star is a point and the comparison is the identity on $Y_0$, not a comparison with an empty product.

source.place: Definition 2.1; coordinate verification of the generalized-operad assertion, following Gepner–Haugseng, arXiv:1312.3178, Definition 3.1.13 and Remarks 4.1.2–4.1.4.

proof.text: The inner fibration and inert lifts of step 1, Segal equivalences of step 2, Kan degree-zero fiber, and mapping-space incidence equivalences of steps 3–5 are precisely all the generalized nonsymmetric operad requirements of [lem-coef-operadic-algebra-presentability]. No nonemptiness was used. If $X=\varnothing$, every fiber $X^{n+1}$ is empty since $n+1>0$, the Segal limits are empty (including the degree-zero identity), and there are no source and target tuples for the quantified mapping assertion. For nonempty $X$, individual $Y_j$ may still be empty when endpoints lie in distinct components; the explicit retractions and homotopies in step 5 remain defined and require no choice of a path. Thus the proof includes these cases and $n=0$.

title: Tuple left fibration satisfies the generalized operad axioms
statement:
Use the universes, Kan spaces and specified tuple relative nerve of [def-coef-complete-algebroid] and the space-valued left-fibration classification of [lem-coef-space-transport-classification]. Fix a small Kan space $X$. The left fibration
$$\Delta_X^{\mathrm{op}}\longrightarrow\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$$
classified by the functor $[n]\mapsto X^{n+1}$ is a generalized nonsymmetric infinity operad in the convention of [lem-coef-operadic-algebra-presentability]. Its degree-zero fibre is the Kan space $X$; inert maps have cocartesian lifts; and for every $n$ the Segal map to the product of the consecutive edge fibres over the shared vertex fibres is an equivalence (with the zero-edge case the identity of $X$). For every $[m]\xrightarrow{\phi}[n]$, source tuple $a$ and target tuple $b$, the mapping space over $\phi$ is the path space from $\phi_*a$ to $b$ in $X^{n+1}$. The incidence diagram formed from all vertex and consecutive-edge inert projections has limit equal to this path space, coordinate by coordinate. These assertions remain valid when $X$ is empty and when $n=0$.
